title: Control of Fire
description: Mastery of fire enabled cooking, warmth, and protection, fundamentally altering human diet and social behaviour.

title: Agriculture
description: The deliberate cultivation of plants in the Fertile Crescent enabled permanent settlements and population growth.

title: Domestication of Animals
description: Taming animals for labour, food, and companionship transformed farming productivity and transportation.

title: Pottery
description: Ceramic vessels allowed food storage, cooking, and water transport, supporting larger settled communities.

title: The Wheel
description: Invented in Mesopotamia for pottery and later transport, the wheel became foundational to mechanical engineering.

title: Writing (Cuneiform)
description: Sumerian cuneiform was among the earliest writing systems, enabling record-keeping, law, and literature.

title: Bronze Metallurgy
description: Alloying copper with tin produced bronze, harder than either constituent, revolutionising tools and weapons.

title: Egyptian Pyramids
description: The Great Pyramids demonstrated advanced engineering, mathematics, and large-scale labour organisation.

title: Babylonian Mathematics
description: Babylonians developed a base-60 number system, quadratic equations, and early algebra on clay tablets.

title: Iron Smelting
description: Iron tools and weapons surpassed bronze in availability and durability, transforming agriculture and warfare.

title: Phoenician Alphabet
description: A compact consonantal alphabet that became the ancestor of Greek, Latin, Arabic, and Hebrew scripts.

title: Greek Democracy
description: Athenian democratic reforms under Cleisthenes established citizen participation in governance, influencing political theory for millennia.

title: Greek Philosophy (Pre-Socratics)
description: Thales, Anaximander, and Heraclitus sought natural explanations for phenomena, founding Western philosophy and science.

title: Pythagorean Theorem
description: Pythagoras formalised the relationship between sides of a right triangle, a cornerstone of geometry and mathematics.

title: Hippocratic Medicine
description: Hippocrates separated medicine from religion, emphasising observation and clinical documentation of disease.

title: Platonic Philosophy
description: Plato's theory of Forms, his Academy, and dialogues shaped Western metaphysics, epistemology, and political philosophy.

title: Aristotelian Logic
description: Aristotle's syllogistic logic and systematic classification of knowledge dominated Western thought for two thousand years.

title: Euclidean Geometry
description: Euclid's Elements axiomatised geometry, providing a model of deductive reasoning used until the 19th century.

title: Archimedean Mechanics
description: Archimedes discovered the lever principle, buoyancy, and methods anticipating integral calculus.

title: Roman Concrete and Engineering
description: Roman opus caementicium enabled domes, aqueducts, and roads that endured millennia, advancing civil engineering.

title: Papermaking
description: Cai Lun refined paper production in Han China, making writing materials cheap and enabling widespread literacy.

title: Ptolemaic Astronomy
description: Ptolemy's Almagest modelled planetary motion with epicycles, dominating astronomy for 1400 years.

title: Compass
description: Chinese lodestone compasses enabled reliable navigation, later transforming global maritime exploration.

title: Algebra (Al-Khwarizmi)
description: Al-Khwarizmi's systematic treatment of linear and quadratic equations founded algebra as a discipline.

title: Gunpowder
description: Discovered in Tang Dynasty China, gunpowder transformed warfare and eventually led to firearms and explosives.

title: Universities
description: The University of Bologna and subsequent European universities institutionalised higher learning and scholarly communities.

title: Optics (Ibn al-Haytham)
description: The Book of Optics established experimental methodology and the intromission theory of vision.

title: Mechanical Clock
description: Mechanical clocks enabled precise timekeeping, transforming navigation, science, and daily life.

title: Printing Press
description: Gutenberg's movable-type press made books affordable, accelerating the spread of knowledge and the Reformation.

title: Copernican Heliocentrism
description: Copernicus placed the Sun at the centre of the solar system, challenging Ptolemaic geocentrism and transforming astronomy.

title: Anatomical Science (Vesalius)
description: De Humani Corporis Fabrica corrected Galenic errors through direct dissection, founding modern anatomy.

title: Telescope
description: The telescope enabled observation of celestial bodies, confirming heliocentrism and revealing new phenomena.

title: Galilean Mechanics
description: Galileo established kinematics through experiments on falling bodies and inclined planes, founding experimental physics.

title: Kepler's Laws of Planetary Motion
description: Kepler discovered that planets move in ellipses with the Sun at one focus, replacing circular orbits.

title: Scientific Method (Bacon/Descartes)
description: Bacon's empiricism and Descartes' rationalism formalised systematic approaches to acquiring knowledge through observation and reason.

title: Calculus
description: Newton and Leibniz independently developed calculus, providing the mathematical language for describing change and motion.

title: Newtonian Mechanics
description: Newton's Principia unified terrestrial and celestial mechanics through three laws of motion and universal gravitation.

title: Microscope and Cell Theory
description: Hooke's Micrographia revealed cells; van Leeuwenhoek observed microorganisms, founding microbiology.

title: Steam Engine
description: Newcomen's atmospheric engine, refined by Watt, powered the Industrial Revolution by converting heat to mechanical work.

title: Linnean Taxonomy
description: Linnaeus introduced binomial nomenclature, providing a universal system for classifying all living organisms.

title: Lagrangian Mechanics
description: Lagrange reformulated Newtonian mechanics using the principle of least action and generalised coordinates.

title: Vaccination
description: Jenner demonstrated that cowpox inoculation prevented smallpox, founding immunology and saving millions of lives.

title: Volta's Battery
description: The voltaic pile provided the first continuous source of electric current, enabling electrochemistry and electrical research.

title: Thermodynamics
description: Clausius and Kelvin formalised energy conservation and entropy, explaining the limits of heat engines and natural processes.

title: Theory of Evolution
description: Darwin's natural selection explained the diversity of life, unifying biology and transforming our understanding of nature.

title: Germ Theory of Disease
description: Pasteur and Koch demonstrated that microorganisms cause disease, revolutionising medicine and public health.

title: Classical Electromagnetism (Maxwell's Equations)
description: Maxwell unified electricity, magnetism, and optics into four equations, predicting electromagnetic waves.

title: Periodic Table
description: Mendeleev arranged elements by atomic weight and properties, predicting undiscovered elements and unifying chemistry.

title: Telephone
description: Bell's telephone converted sound to electrical signals and back, enabling real-time long-distance voice communication.

title: Statistical Mechanics
description: Boltzmann connected thermodynamic entropy to microscopic states, bridging mechanics and thermodynamics statistically.

title: Electric Power Systems
description: Edison and Tesla developed generation and distribution of electricity, powering cities and industry.

title: Internal Combustion Engine
description: Otto's four-stroke engine enabled automobiles and aircraft, transforming transportation and industry.

title: Radio
description: Marconi demonstrated wireless telegraphy using electromagnetic waves, founding broadcast communication.

title: X-rays
description: Roentgen discovered X-rays, enabling medical imaging and advancing atomic physics.

title: Powered Flight
description: The Wright brothers achieved sustained controlled powered flight, inaugurating the aviation age.

title: Special Relativity
description: Einstein showed that space and time are relative and the speed of light is constant, yielding E=mc^2.

title: General Relativity
description: Einstein's geometric theory of gravity described spacetime curvature caused by mass-energy, predicting black holes and gravitational waves.

title: Antibiotics (Penicillin)
description: Fleming's discovery of penicillin launched the antibiotic era, saving millions from bacterial infections.

title: Quantum Mechanics
description: Heisenberg and Schrodinger formulated quantum mechanics, describing matter and energy at atomic scales with wave functions and uncertainty.

title: Nuclear Fission
description: Hahn and Strassmann split uranium atoms, releasing enormous energy and enabling nuclear power and weapons.

title: Turing Machine / Computation Theory
description: Turing defined a universal model of computation, establishing the theoretical foundations of computer science.

title: Electronic Computer
description: ENIAC and subsequent von Neumann architecture machines enabled general-purpose programmable computation.

title: Quantum Field Theory
description: QFT combined quantum mechanics and special relativity, describing particles as excitations of underlying fields.

title: Transistor
description: The transistor replaced vacuum tubes, enabling miniaturised, reliable electronics and the semiconductor revolution.

title: Structure of DNA
description: Watson and Crick determined DNA's double helix, revealing the molecular basis of heredity and launching molecular biology.

title: Satellites and Space Exploration
description: Sputnik demonstrated orbital spaceflight, launching the space age and enabling global communications and GPS.

title: Integrated Circuit
description: Kilby and Noyce combined multiple transistors on one chip, enabling microprocessors and modern electronics.

title: Laser
description: Stimulated emission of coherent light enabled precision measurement, telecommunications, surgery, and data storage.

title: The Internet (ARPANET)
description: Packet-switched networking connected distant computers, evolving into the global Internet.

title: Standard Model of Particle Physics
description: The Standard Model unified electromagnetic, weak, and strong forces, classifying all known fundamental particles.

title: Personal Computer
description: Affordable microcomputers brought computing to homes and small businesses, democratising information technology.

title: World Wide Web
description: Berners-Lee's hypertext system made the Internet accessible to everyone, transforming communication, commerce, and culture.

title: Global Positioning System (GPS)
description: A constellation of satellites providing precise geolocation, transforming navigation, logistics, and surveying.

title: Human Genome Project
description: Complete sequencing of the human genome opened personalised medicine, gene therapy, and evolutionary genomics.

title: Smartphone
description: The iPhone and subsequent smartphones combined computing, internet, GPS, and telephony in a pocket device, reshaping society.

title: CRISPR Gene Editing
description: CRISPR-Cas9 enabled precise, programmable editing of DNA, revolutionising genetics, medicine, and agriculture.

title: Deep Learning / Artificial Intelligence
description: Deep neural networks achieved superhuman performance in image recognition, launching modern AI applications across all fields.

title: Gravitational Wave Detection
description: LIGO's detection of gravitational waves confirmed a century-old prediction of general relativity and opened a new observational window.

title: Renewable Energy at Scale
description: Solar and wind power reached cost parity with fossil fuels, enabling global transition toward sustainable energy systems.

title: Large Language Models
description: Transformer-based language models demonstrated general-purpose reasoning and generation, transforming how humans interact with AI.
